title: UK CPI, October 2027 (ONS, 07:00 London) — the upward electricity-VAT base effect nobody diarised, because the cut it reverses never showed up as a fall
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukoctober2027, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads 'Consumer price inflation, UK: October 2027', 'Release date: 17 November 2027 7:00am', and states 'This release is not yet published'. ONS's own label on the entry is Provisional. Filed estimate on that label, on this lane's no-self-confirm limit, and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. Proposed by uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01, 2026-09-09; canonical file written by the never-assessed initial research, 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/uk-cpi-2027-11-17.from-uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01.json (read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). The proposal's placement finding stands and is confirmed from primaries: SI 2026/987 (legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/987/made, fetched) zero-rates GB domestic electricity 'beginning with 1st October 2026 and ending with 31st March 2027', so this print measures a 5%-rated October against a ZERO-RATED base month and carries +5.0000% (5/100) on the CPI electricity index from tax alone, running through the March 2028 print. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS ENTRY EARNS ITS PLACE: the base effect is unusually well hidden, because the cut that created it left NO VISIBLE FOOTPRINT. Ofgem's 26-Aug-2026 cap release (fetched) says 'The Government's decision to remove VAT from all domestic electricity bills is reflected in this update' and that electricity-only households 'will see a much smaller INCREASE of less than 1%' — an increase, after the relief. So the net-of-VAT electricity price rose roughly 5% on the same date the 4.7619% cut landed, and the October 2026 electricity index should print roughly flat-to-up, not down. There is no October 2026 plunge for anyone to remember, so a forecaster reading the observed base sees nothing anomalous in it. SIZE: 2027 CJXA weight x 5.0%. CJXA fetched direct today reads 27.0 (2023), 23.3142 (2024), 19.1488 (2025), 20.6065 (2026); the 2027 weight is undrawn until the January print on 2027-02-17 and is price-updated to a ZERO-RATED December 2026 (ONS CPI technical manual, fetched), which shaves ~4.76% off it. This lane's tighter band is 18.0-21.5/1000 => +0.090 to +0.108pp on headline, inside and in the lower half of the proposing lane's 0.091-0.129pp. THE CONFOUND STRUCTURE IS CLEANER THAN THE APRIL SIBLING'S: VAT is back at 5% from April 2027, so this print's MONTH-ON-MONTH electricity move is pure Oct-Dec 2027 Ofgem cap reset and the VAT step sits entirely in the ANNUAL comparison, where dividing by 1.05 isolates it — where uk-cpi-2027-05-19 mixes VAT and a cap reset in the same m/m. SEQUENCING (BoE upcoming-MPC-dates page, fetched, '2027 provisional dates'): MPC + Monetary Policy Report 2027-11-04, thirteen days BEFORE this print — the identical geometry to uk-cpi-2026-11-18 and the 2026-11-05 MPR — then MPC 2027-12-16, with the November print landing 2027-12-15 the morning before it. So the Bank must FORECAST this base effect and the tape must remember it thirteen months on; the asymmetry, not the number, is the finding. ATTRIBUTION RULE: check the ONS contributions table for the electricity contribution before treating an autumn 2027 UK upside surprise as inflation news or as a hawkish surprise the December MPC can act on. VOIDED IF THE ZERO RATE IS EXTENDED beyond 2027-03-31 (FT-uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01-1, score by 2027-03-31); the first venue that could do it is the 2026-10-28 Budget. Its real job is attribution, on a 2027-11-17 that also carries FOMC minutes and a VIX expiration, with opex 2027-11-19. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
